issues.summary: compute_weeks_complete (line 92): the `paging.truncated` branch is the ONLY zero-declare path that returns [], [] without printing a warning. Every sibling degrade path (paging missing, rows < matched, matched == 0, totalOrdersScanned == 0, emptyRangeWithInvalidLabels) prints '[shopspend] WARNING: ... zero weeks declared'. On a truncated pull the operator sees only '[shopspend] posted N row(s)' and exit 0, with absence detection silently disabled for the whole pull. No test asserts a warning here either — test_gate_truncated_response_declares_zero_weeks checks the return value only, while every sibling has a matching *_warns test. Data integrity is unaffected (the safe outcome is correct and `truncated` still lands in the ShopSpendPulls row); this is a diagnostics/consistency gap in a phase whose stated purpose is making degraded modes loud.

Line 85: the degraded-mode log reads 'weeks_complete absent — tombstoning skipped entirely for this pull', but ingestShopSpendRows is per-REQUEST, not per-pull. In a normal chunked pull, post_pull deliberately posts split weeks and undeclared weeks in requests that carry no weeks_complete, so this line fires on every such chunk even though the pull's other chunks declared their weeks correctly. An operator reading the GAS execution log would conclude absence detection was off for the entire pull. Suggest 'for this request' and naming the row count.

isValidWeekLabelArray_ (line 208) validates week labels with /^\d{4}-W\d{2}$/, which accepts 2026-W00, 2026-W54..2026-W99. The Python CLI's _week_label (runner.py) deliberately bounds the week number to 01-53 with the comment that unbounded labels 'survive argparse, flow into iso_week_span, and get declared complete'. GAS is the destructive side (it is what actually tombstones) and is the looser of the two validators. Impact today is nil — a phantom label matches no sheet row, so it produces no tombstone candidates — but the guard on the authoritative side is weaker than the guard on the advisory side.

Line 165 documents a curl that mass-tombstones a week by naming it in both weeks_complete and weeks_verified_empty with rows: [], bypassing the blast-radius breaker. doPost has no write-side token check (unlike doGet's checkReadToken_), so this breaker-bypass primitive is reachable by any unauthenticated caller who knows the /exec URL. The pre-diff code was equally destructive (tombstoning was scoped to weeks seen in rows, with no breaker at all), so this is not a regression — the diff net-adds a defence plus a documented bypass — but the bypass is now a written-down, copy-pasteable procedure against an unauthenticated endpoint. Worth a follow-up to gate doPost on a shared write token.
